Q. 4 اِسْبَكَرَّ i. q. اِسْبَطَرَّ in its several significations: (K:) i. e. (TA) ―
-b2- He stretched himself: (TA:) he lay upon his side, and stretched himself: (AA, S, TA:) [&c.] ―
-b3- He (a youth, or young man,) became tall: (Lh:) and اسبكرّت She (a girl) became of erect and justly-proportioned stature. (S, K.) An ex. occurs in a verse of Imra-el-Keys, cited voce مِجْوَلٌ. (S.) ―
-b4- It (a plant) became tall and full-grown: (TA:) and it (anything) became extended, and long, or tall. (Lh.) ―
-b5- He went at random, or heedlessly; without consideration, or certain aim. (Lh.) ―
-b6- It (a river) flowed. (TA.) ―
-b7- اسبكرّت عَيْنُهُ His eye shed tears. (Lh.) But ISd says that this is not known in classical Arabic. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
